extracted.intended_audience: publishers, journal editors, librarians, researchers, and organizations involved in scholarly communication and peer review
extracted.subtask_description: Announcing and describing the ANSI/NISO Z39.106-2023 Peer Review Terminology Standard intended to harmonize vocabulary for peer review of articles and journals to improve transparency and comparability across publications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simplified terminology for peer review roles and practices
rubrics_metrics.description: ANSI/NISO Z39.106-2023 offers a simplified terminology that will make the peer review process more transparent to authors, reviewers, and readers across the journals that adopt it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a shared, simplified set of terms to describe peer review roles and practices so stakeholders (authors, reviewers, readers) can understand what processes were used; promotes clearer communication and reduces ambiguity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standardize nomenclature to enable comparability
rubrics_metrics.description: A shared set of definitions will also enable the community to compare peer review processes across publications more easily.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt the standard definitions so that peer review models and procedures can be compared between journals and publishers; consistency across publications is a key objective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support open research and foster transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: The standard will support open research by simplifying the communication of peer review roles and practices and fostering greater transparency in the peer review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Framing and publishing peer review practices in these standardized terms is intended to address concerns about fairness and to increase trust in scholarly communication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope: developed for articles and journal publications
rubrics_metrics.description: The new standard was developed for articles and journal publications, and a NISO Standing Committee may address books and other peer-reviewed research content in future.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Current applicability is to article- and journal-level peer review; implementers should note that other content types (e.g., books) are not yet covered by this standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Freely available standard to encourage adoption
rubrics_metrics.description: The Peer Review Terminology Standard is freely available at https://www.niso.org/standards-committees/peer-review-terminology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Making the standard freely accessible is intended to facilitate easy adoption and promulgation across publishers and journals; implementers can access and reference it without paywall barriers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence-based development through working groups and trials
rubrics_metrics.description: The standard was developed building on STM's initial set of definitions and best practices, with many pre-publication trials at publishers providing practical information and input from STM and NISO working groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adoption and interpretation should consider that the terminology reflects consensus and lessons from trials and working-group inputs; implementers can rely on this provenance when integrating the standard into workflows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strengthen trust via cooperation and open dialogue
rubrics_metrics.description: Strengthening overall trust in scholarly communication—in this case, the peer review process—through cooperation and open dialogue is cited as a role of NISO standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the standard as a tool to foster cooperative efforts among stakeholders (publishers, librarians, researchers) and to promote transparent conversations about peer review practices.
